headline: Approved Popeyes at 584 Alfred Street and several other site plans; denied day care at 123 Summer Street; tabled UNE pier extension.
summary: Approved site plans for Popeyes at 584 Alfred Street, a parking lot at 41 Main Street, and a cold storage addition at 18 Morin Street. Denied a day care permit at 123 Summer Street by a 3-1 vote. Tabled a one-year extension for a University of New England marine research pier at 11 Hills Beach Road until the Saco River Corridor Commission votes.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 5, 2026 meeting unanimously.
Denied a conditional use permit for a day care at 123 Summer Street, 3-1 vote.
Approved the final site plan for a 2,536-square-foot Popeyes at 584 Alfred Street, with two waivers and conditions, unanimous vote.
Tabled the one-year extension request from the University of New England for its marine research pier until the Saco River Corridor Commission votes, 3-1 vote.
Approved a conditional use permit for a Private Non-Medical Institute for under 16 people at 13 Crescent Street, unanimous vote.
Approved a shoreland permit to rebuild a dwelling within its existing footprint at 67 Fortunes Rocks Road, unanimous vote.
Approved the final site plan for a 54-space parking lot at 41 Main Street, unanimous vote.
Approved a site plan amendment for a 2,310-square-foot cold storage addition at 18 Morin Street, unanimous vote.
Approved a conditional use and site plan amendment for Haley Properties, LLC at 539 Elm Street, with a buffer waiver and fence condition, unanimous vote.

PLANNING BOARD MEETING MINUTES 
August 19, 2026 
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance-Meeting brought to order at 6:00 PM 
2. Declaration of Quorum 
Planning Board: John McCurry, Matthew Sargent-Dubois, Roch Angers, Leah Schaffer, 
Chico Potvin & Rob Nicoll (Alternate Member)  
Staff: David Galbraith & Nan Whitten 
Harry Center Legal Counsel to the City 
3. Adjustments to Agenda 
7G will be presented first, 7C will be presented second, then the agenda will be followed by 
unfinished business. 
4. Planner’s Business 
Meeting Minutes from August 4, 2026, Internal Development Review Meeting 
      5. Consent Agenda 
 5.a. Approval of Meeting Minutes of August 5, 2026  
 MOTIONS: 6:02 PM 
 Motion-Angers-Motion to approve Meeting Minutes as presented 
 Second-Schaffer 
 Vote: Motion passed unanimously 
6. Unfinished Business 
6.a. 2026.20 Review of a project for Bakhita Saabino at 123 Summer Street (Tax Map 35, 
Lot 28) in the R-2 zone. This project was originally approved on June 17, 2026. On July 1, 
2026, the Planning Board voted to re-review this project. Applicant wants to open a 
licensed day care in her home at 123 Summer Street. 
• Applicant was not at meeting 
MOTIONS: 7:46 PM 
Motion-Sargent-Dubois-Motion to take project off the table 
Second-Angers 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
• Angers stated that he has gone to the site on 4 different occasions and does not think 
it is safe for daycare, there are no sidewalks, not enough room for a play area on the 
site.  He will not vote for approval. 
• Galbraith read the information received from DHS 
• Potvin does not think that DHS has looked at the site and that they are being 
lackadaisical.    Potvin does not feel like it is a safe site and the schedule submitted 
by the applicant does not make sense.  He does not think the Fire Department went 
by and looked at the site.  Potvin will not approve.
• Nicoll feels that there is more than one way that the Board could make this right. He 
hears the Board’s concerns but feels like the Board is getting into areas that are 
beyond their purview.  Nicoll stated that he feels the Board is making things 
difficult.  The site is not in the highest traffic parts of the City, and it could work. 
• Schaffer said that she has walked the site to the Rec Center 4 times also and feels 
that the staff to child ratio makes it safe.  It is not the ideal spot but it’s hard to say 
that this wouldn’t work. 
• Potvin feels that the Board’s decisions are being heavily scrutinized.  He took his 
wife to the site and told her about walking the children to the Martin Center and as 
an experienced daycare provider her opinion was no.  The City Council is adamant 
on safety and sidewalks this is scenario is in opposition to the Council’s leadership.  
He brought up another daycare situation a few years ago that the Board denied for 
the same reasons.  Potvin said he has a bad feeling about this project and that this is 
a bad location. 
8:02 PM  
Motion-Anger-Motion to deny project #2026.20 a Conditional Use Permit for 
Bakhita Saabino to open a day care called Helping Hand Learning at 123 Summer 
Street (Tax Map 35, Lot 48) within the Residential 2 zone due to safety issues getting 
to a play area and a lack of play space on the site. 
Second-Potvin 
Vote-Motion passed 3-1 (Sargent-Dubois, Angers & Potvin in favor, Schaffer 
opposed) 
      7. New Business 
7.g 2026.01 Final Plan Review for Golden Chicken of Biddeford, LLC (Popeyes) to open a 
                  Fast Food Restaurant at 584 Alfred Street (Tax Map 2, Lot 23) in the B-2 zone. 
• Galbraith introduced the project 
• Galbraith explained that the Traffic Movement Permit from the State is being 
wrapped up now and will be sent to the City soon. 
NO PUBLIC COMMENTS 
MOTIONS: 6:10 
Motion-Angers-Motion to Approve Case # 2026.01 Final Site Plan Review for Golden 
Chicken of Biddeford, LLC for a proposed 2,536 SF Popeye’s Fast-Food restaurant located 
at 584 Alfred Street (Tax Map 2, Lot 23) within the B-2 Zone, with the adoption of the 
recommended / attached Conditions of Approval (COA) in addition to granting the below 
waivers: 
1) Section 5.B.(i)(3) (hardscape to occupy more than 30% of the proposed developed area). 
2) Article VI Performance Standards Section 29 Erosion Control 1. A 1.5:1 riprap slope is 
proposed to extend over the easterly property line. 
Conditions of Approval: 
1. Standard Conditions of Approval apply. 
2. Bonding and Inspection Fees: Bonding and inspection fees shall be established and 
submitted prior to the pre-construction meeting.
3. Traffic Movement Permit (TMP): A signed copy of the Maine Department of 
Transportation Traffic Movement Permit (TMP) shall be submitted to the City Planner 
and Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of the required Occupancy Permits. 
4. Sprinkler Design: The sprinkler design must be submitted to the State Fire Marshall’s 
Office (SFMO) for review and approval. 
5. Fire Hydrant Testing: The project includes a private on-site fire hydrant to serve the 
site. The Fire Department will require a flow rating test of the on-site hydrant and copies of 
the test reports supporting the development shall be submitted to the Fire Department and 
Planning Department prior to the issuance of an Occupancy Permit. 
6. Modifications to Approved Development Plans: The project shall be constructed 
according to the approved development plans. If any site changes are desired, the applicant 
must submit a letter requesting a “Minor Modification” to the approved development 
plans. The applicant must adequately justify the reasons for those deviations. The 
narrative shall include the current approved plans and the proposed modifications, which 
the City Planner shall agree to in writing before construction. Changes beyond the 
authority of the City Planner or modification deemed not be “minor” shall be reviewed and 
approved by the Planning Board prior to being constructed. 
7. As-built Drawings: Once the As-Built drawings are submitted to the Planning 
Department (clearly identifying what deviations and variances were installed based on the 
approved permit drawings), the City Engineering Department will conduct an inspection. 
The “as-built Checklist” shall be submitted for review and approval prior to the final 
performance guarantee release. 
8. As-built drawings and CAD Files: As-built drawings and CAD Files must be submitted 
to the Planning & Engineering Departments before a ‘Site Punchlist Inspection’ and any 
bond release. 
9. York County Recorded Drawings: The applicant must submit recorded copies, from the 
York County Registry of Deeds, of the Planning Board signed site plan drawings to the 
Planning & Engineering Departments prior to the issuance of any building permits for the 
project. Signed and recorded copies shall include all stipulated Conditions of Approval 
(COA). 
10. Alfred Street Sidewalk: The Applicant will be responsible for installing the sidewalk 
along their Alfred Street frontage. This should be coordinated with the City’s Engineering 
Department. 
11. Thatcher Brook Watershed Impact Fee: The property is located within Thatcher Brook 
Watershed so is subject to the related impact fees which will be paid prior to the issuance 
of a building permit. The fee will be calculated by the City’s City Planner prior to the 
scheduling of the required pre-construction meeting. 
12. Grease Trap and Chiller: The project will require a grease trap with a chiller, to 
solidify grease within the trap, prior discharging into the sanitary sewer. A fats, oils and 
grease (FOG) permit shall be issued prior to the issuance of an Occupancy Permit. 
13. Signage: The application includes a detailed signage program. These should be 
reviewed by the Board for illustrative purposes only. All signage shall conform to the City’s
sign ordinance and will be reviewed for conformity by the City’s Code Office at the time of 
building and signage permit review and issuance. 
14. Sewer Permit Fee: Sewer Permit fee shall be paid to the City’s Engineering Department 
prior to Building Permit issuance. The fee shall be calculated by the City’s Engineering 
Department prior to the scheduling of the required pre-construction meeting. 
15. Alfred Street Crosswalk Improvements: Prior to the issuance of any building permits 
for the project, the applicant shall contribute $37,500. for their proportionate share of the 
Alfred Street crosswalk improvements. 
16. Alfred Street Traffic Signal Improvements: Prior to the issuance of any building 
permits for the project, the applicant shall contribute $40,000. for their proportionate 
share of the Alfred Street mast and mast arm installation, associated traffic signal 
improvements, and associated lighting and wiring. 
17. Nighttime Construction: The project will require nightwork construction for their 
proposed off-site utility connections. Construction and lane closures shall be limited 
between the hours of 9:30 pm to 6:00 am. A minimum of one lane of travel, in each 
direction, shall be always maintained during construction. All off-site work and lane 
closures shall be coordinated and approved by the City’s Public Works Director and 
Engineering Director prior to the commencement of any off-site work. 
18. Traffic Control Plan: A formal traffic control plan shall be submitted prior to the 
required preconstruction meeting, documenting lane closures, signage, and flagging. The 
plan shall be reviewed and approved by the City’s Public Works Director and Engineering 
Director prior to the commencement of any off-site work. 
19. Off-site Trench Work: One continuous surface trench cap shall be paved for all utility 
connections, matching arterial road gravel and pavement depths listed in Table 62A of the 
City’s Ordinance and shall be in full compliance with Maine Department of 
Transportation (MDOT) Utility Accommodation Rules, Section 6(D) paving specification 
sheet. Where discrepancies may occur the City’s Public Works Director shall make the 
final determination, following consultation with MDOT. 
20. Traffic Movement Permit (TMP): A signed copy of the required Traffic Movement 
Permit (TMP), issued by the Maine Department of Transportation (MDOT) shall be 
submitted to the Planning Department, Engineering Department and Code Enforcement 
Department prior to the scheduling of the required pre-construction meeting. 
21. Deliveries: All deliveries occurring to the site shall be limited between the hours of 9:00 
pm to 5:00 am. 
22. Fire Department Connection (FDC): The project shall include a 5” Storz Fire 
Department Connection (FDC). 
23. All required inspections be completed 
Second- Potvin 
Vote- Motion passed unanimously 
 
7.c.   2026.44 Review of a request from University of New England (UNE) to receive a 1-
year extension of their 2025 approval to construct a Marine Science Research Pier at 11 
Hills Beach Road (Tax Map 52, Lot 4) in the Institutional Zone.
• Galbraith explained that this item was moved up so that City Solicitor will not be at 
the meeting until the last item. 
• Galbraith explained that this approval is expiring due to litigation and the Saco 
River Corridor Commission (SRCC). 
• Angers stated that the SRCC is meeting next Thursday to decide on whether they 
will give UNE an extension on the SRCC approval.  He would like this decision to be 
tabled until after the SRCC votes.  He also wants to read and absorb what the 
SRCC meeting minutes say. 
• Center said that the moratorium was sent to court on 6-30-26.  The judge stayed it, 
so the approval stands.  If the extension is denied Attorney Center will be hard 
pressed to defend the decision. Tabling this will not change the original decision, 
that ship has sailed. 
• Schaffer explained that the Board is voting on an extension, not renegotiating the 
project from the beginning. 
• Potvin said the 250’ buffer is an ordinance or law or understanding and the Board 
needs to follow the ordinance. 
• Center explained that neither ordinance from the City nor SRCC are clear. 
• Potvin feels he must follow Angers lead until the buffer gets figured out. 
• Nicoll looked at the 2001 ordinance in question, and it is not part of the City’s code.  
He feels this extension is like other extensions they have granted where funding is 
not in place yet.  This was not UNE’s fault, this is not our responsibility. 
• Potvin wants to know if this will impact their timeline.  He does not want them to 
have to reapply. 
• Center answered that no, this will not negatively impact their timeline, but it is 
sending a statement. If UNE does not get SRCC approval, this will become a 
Planning issue. 
MOTIONS: 6:23 pm 
Motion-Angers-Motion to table the 1-year extension for UNE until SRCC votes on 
the request by UNE 
Second-Potvin 
Vote-Motion passed 3-1 (Sargent-Dubois, Angers & Potvin in favor, Schaffer 
opposed) 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
7.a 2026.39 The Biddeford Planning Board will review a Conditional Use Permit request 
                  from Salvatore Saccareli to open a Private Non-Medical Institute (PNMI) for under 16     
                  people at 13 Crescent Street (Tax Map 38, Lot 292) in the MSRD-2 zone. This business   
       is currently a sober living boarding house run by Mr. Saccareli. 
• Galbraith introduced the project he mentioned that the structure does not have 
parking issues as the clients rarely have licenses or cars. 
• Joseph Lantz and Nate Roberts represented the applicants.
• Roberts is with Portland Treatment where they provide clinical services so that 
people have more resources who are struggling and that is what they will be 
bringing to this business. 
• Angers asked why they came to Biddeford. 
• Lantz answered it is because it is needed in Biddeford and the building they own 
in Biddeford is perfect for this business.   
• Angers asked about their success rate. They have a very good success rate in this 
field with 15-18% of their clients making it to a year of sobriety.  York County is 
severely under serviced in this field especially compared to Cumberland County. 
• Angers asked them to explain their treatment process which they did and 
explained the staffing of the facility. 
• Angers asked them about parking issues; they answered that their clients would 
not have cars because most of them would not have licenses. 
• Schaffer asked if this application would be changing the conditional use and if 
they would be proposing ramps outside.  She wanted to make sure they knew 
that if they were changing the building on the outside, they would have to get 
Historic Preservation Committee approval also. 
• Nicoll asked about bike storage.  The answer is yes there is bike storage as most 
of their clients ride bikes to get around.  They also have a transport vehicle to 
take the clients on outings such as hiking and such. 
• Potvin asked how the facility is funded.  After 1 month the clients must pay rent 
or use General Assistance. 
• Sargent-Dubois asked about client turn over.  It will be every 3-6 months, once 
they get up and running it will be more staggered. 
• Sargent-Dubois asked how they handle crisis situations.  The staff is trained in 
crisis situations so normally it is all handled in house unless it is something that 
is beyond the regular crises. 
• McCurry asked about the condition of the clients when they first got to the 
house. They must be through detox already.  If they have not been through detox 
the staff finds detox for them and gets them there, this happens daily.  How these 
people are charged for medical care and detoxes goes through Maine Care and 
the home helps those who need it get signed up. 
MOTIONS: 6:49 pm 
Motion-Schaffer- Motion to Approve Case # 2026.39 a Conditional Use Permit 
(CUP) request from Salvatore Saccareli to open a Private Non-Medical Institute 
(PNMI) facility for under 16 people at 13 Crescent Street (Tax Map 38, Lot 292) 
in the MSRD-2 zone, with the below recommended Conditions of Approval 
(COA). 
1. The project shall adhere to National Fire Protection Association Life Safety 
Code and other fire- and life-safety requirements. 
2. A full fire alarm system shall be installed at the location to the satisfaction of 
the State Fire Marshall’s Office (SFMO) and the Biddeford Fire Chief.
3. A full sprinkler system shall be installed at the location to the satisfaction of 
the State Fire Marshall’s Office (SFMO) and the Biddeford Fire Chief. 
4. The Applicant shall provide the City’s Planning Department and Code 
Enforcement Department copies of all required / approved State licenses prior to 
an Occupancy Permit, for the proposed use, is issued. 
5. The Applicant shall apply to the HPC with any exterior changes as necessary. 
Second-Angers 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
PUBLIC COMMENTS 
Steve Guay-Ward 7 
 7.b 2026.31 Review of the Shoreland Permit Application for Michelle Shekarchi to 
complete construction of a pile-supported foundation and a new dwelling which will 
generally be rebuilt within the existing structure's footprint at the site and will not increase 
overall impervious cover. The project is located at 67 Fortunes Rocks Road (Tax Map 64, 
Lot 43) in the Coastal Residential and Limited Residential zones. This project began in 
2024, but architectural and engineering delays have caused the applicant to re-apply for 
the shoreland permit. 
• Galbraith introduced the project. 
• Angela Blanchette represented the applicants via TEAMS 
• Schaffer confirmed that the original permit was for the seawall and now the 
applicant is focusing on the house.  She asked questions about the boxes on the plan. 
• The applicants are working very closely with Roby Fecteau 
• Schaffer reminded the applicants that they will need a DEP permit where the 
property is in the dunes.  It was determined that they do not need such permit 
because the structure is going to be on pilings. 
• Nicoll confirmed that the new structure will be built within the footprint, it may be 
smaller or parts outside of the footprint but will generally be in the same place. 
• Angers stated that he was confused, can the footprint be moved?  It may be changed 
but must keep the same square footage. 
• Schaffer clarified the rules about the footprint. 
• Potvin stated that it looks consistent and feels that it is mostly an issue for Roby 
Fecteau and that he has a good handle on it.  
 MOTIONS: 7:10 PM 
 Motion-Angers-Motion to Approve Case # 2026.31 Review a Shoreland Permit request 
from Michelle Skekarchi for a Shoreland Permit seeking Greatest Practical Extent 
(GPE) Determination to rebuild within the existing structure's footprint at the site and 
not increasing the overall impervious cover. The project is located at 67 Fortunes Rocks 
Road (Tax Map 64, Lot 43) in the Coastal Residential & Limited Residential zones, with 
the recommended Conditions of Approval (COA). 
1. The new building shall not be relocated closer to any of the existing property lines as 
noted on the approved plan. 
2. The Code Enforcement Officer shall review and approve conformance to Section 15 of 
the Shoreland Zoning Ordinance.
3. Obtain all required permits from the Maine Department of Environmental Protection 
and the Biddeford Code Enforcement Office. 
4. This approval shall expire one year from the date below if a substantial start is not made 
in construction. If a substantial start (30% of project completion, i.e., framing and 
foundation) is made within one year of the date below, the applicant shall have one 
additional year to complete the project thereinafter; this approval shall expire August 
19, 2027.2. Prior to the issuance of a Building Permit for the proposed single-family 
home, the applicant’s project engineer shall submit a letter to the City’s Planning, Code 
Enforcement and Engineering Departments certifying that the constructed private way 
has been built to the City’s private way standards. This letter shall be signed and 
stamped by the applicant’s project engineer. 
Second-Sargent-Dubois 
PUBLIC COMMENTS 
Mark Robinson Ward 1 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
7.d. 2026.25 The Planning Board will continue to review a Site Plan Application for 41 
Main Street, LLC.  The applicant wants to demolish the existing structure to create 54 
parking spaces.  The address of the property is 41 Main Street (Tax Map 41, Lot 138) in 
the MSRD 1 zone. 
• Galbraith introduced the project and reminded the Board that they received 
Preliminary Approval June 1, 2026. 
• He explained that the plans have been amended to show the changes in the retaining 
wall, curb cuts, landscaping and elevations. 
• To avoid disruption of traffic on Main Street, the team will utilize Emery Street, the 
construction vehicles will not be out front and there will be no disruption of the 
sidewalk.  The applicants will do their best to keep the noise down; this will be a 
quick demo, and they will be in communication with their neighbors and take 
measures to keep the dust and dirt down.   
• There was a question about vermin during the demolition, this is a vacant building, 
there is no food, so no vermin are anticipated. 
• The dumpster will be kept in the parking lot. 
• The applicants will put slats in the surrounding fence to prevent light spread. 
• Nicoll thanked the applicants for the changes, he asked how the tenants would know 
about the parking changes.  Management will notify the tenants of all changes. 
• Potvin sees no anticipated problems with the tear down, asked what the anticipated 
e.t.a. is on the new building, there is no e.t.a. yet. 
• Schaffer told the applicants that the wall was not what she had in mind as the one 
proposed does not tie into downtown.  She wants a natural wall, the applicant said 
the wall proposed is expensive and what Schaffer is proposing will be worse. 
• Schaffer wants to make sure the Historic Preservation Commission has been 
notified of the change. 
• Sargent-Dubois stated that he does not like the wall either.
MOTION: 7:28 PM 
Motion-Potvin- Motion to approve Case # 2026.25 Final Site Plan Review for 41 
Main, LLC for a 54-parking stall parking lot located at 41 Main Street (Map 41 Lot 
138) within the Main Street Revitalization District – 1 (MSRD-1) Zoning District, 
with the attached recommended Conditions of Approval (COA). 
Second-Angers 
PUBLIC COMMENTS 
John Phillips-Ward 2 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
• Sargent-Dubois asked if the HPC approval can be added to the Planning Board 
approval 
• Galbraith to notify Brad Favreau about the changes in the wall 
7.e. 2026.30 The Planning Board will review an application for a Minor Site Plan 
Amendment for Prescott Metals to expand by constructing a 2,310-square-foot cold storage 
facility.  Prescott Metals is located at 18 Morin Street (Tax Map 12, Lot 20) in General 
Industrial Zone 1. 
• Galbraith introduced the project and noted the change in the drive aisle to 1 way to 
accommodate the Fire Department. 
NO PUBLIC COMMENTS 
MOTIONS: 7:34 PM 
Motion-Schaffer- Motion to Approve, Case # 2026.30 Preliminary and Final Site 
Plan Amendment Review for Prescott Metal for the construction of a 2,310 square 
foot cold storage building addition and approval of a waiver to Article VI, Section 
61 (Stormwater Plan Waiver) at 18 Morin Street (Map 12, Lot 20) in the General 
Industrial (I-1) Zone, with the following seven (7) Conditions of Approval (COA): 
1) All previous Conditions of Approval are hereby reaffirmed. 
2) Bonding and Inspection Fees: Bonding and inspection fees shall be 
established prior to scheduling of the required Pre-construction meeting. 
3) Modifications to Approved Development Plans: The project shall be 
constructed in accordance with the approved development plans.  No deviations to 
the approved development plans shall be made without prior written authorization 
by the City Planner. 
4) As Build Drawings:  Once stamped and signed “As-Built drawings” are 
submitted to the Planning and Engineering Departments (clearly identifying what 
approved deviations and variances were installed based on the approved permit 
drawings), the City Engineering Department will conduct an inspection.  The “as 
Built Checklist” shall be submitted for review and approval, for any performance 
guarantee release. 
 
5) As-Built Drawings and CAD Files need to be submitted to the Planning & 
Engineering Departments prior to a ‘Site Punch list Inspection’ and any bond 
release.
6) York County Recorded Drawings: Applicant must submit recorded copies of 
the approved plans, which shall include the listed Conditions of Approval (COA), at 
the York County Registry of Deed drawings to Planning & Engineering Department 
prior to Building Permit Issuance. 
7) Required Inspections:   
i. Erosion & Sediment Control Inspections 
1. Needs to be completed by a City-approved 3rd Party Inspector and paid by 
the Applicant via the inspection fee escrow being held by the City.   
2. The City’s Engineering Department, at minimum, shall be notified of an 
initial E&S inspection prior to breaking ground.   
Second-Sargent-Dubois 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
7.f. 2026.05 The Planning Board will review a Final Site Plan Application for Haley’s 
Properties, LLC at 539 Elm Street (Tax Map 13, Lots 21 & 21-1) in the B-2 zone. The 
proposal is to remove the existing garage to build a showroom and to also build a 
warehouse on the property. 
• Galbraith re-introduced the project 
• Eric Dube from Trillium Engineering stated that there are no changes on the 
previously submitted plans. 
MOTIONS: 7:40 PM 
Motions-Sargent-Dubois- Motion to Approve Case # 2026.05 Final Review for Haley 
Properties, LLC (dba Hayley’s Metal Shop, Inc.) for a Conditional Use (light 
manufacturing) and Site Plan Amendment to an existing Development Plan to 
remove and reconstruct a 1,250 +/- square foot (footprint) detached building and 
construction of a new 3,000 square foot detached building, located at 539 Elm Street 
(Tax Map 13, and Lot 21 and 21-1) located within the B2 (Highway Business) 
Zoning District, with the Staff recommended Conditions of Approval (COA). 
Waiver Request: Motion to Approve Waiver to Article VI – Performance 
Standards, Section 12 – Buffers and Article VI buffer requirements which require a 
30’ wide buffer strip adjacent to residential used/zoned property. I motion to 
approve the proposed waivers with a condition that a 6-foot-high solid screening 
fence is installed on the property line as shown on the Staff exhibit (Page #8 of this 
report) in blue and red. 
Second-Angers 
Vote-Motion passed unanimously 
8. Other Business 
• The Board discussed updates to zones for houses to protect them from storms 
• Schaffer explained the requirements 
9. Adjourn 
 MOTIONS: 8:05 PM 
 Motion-Angers-Motion to adjourn 
 Second-Sargent-Dubois 
 Vote-Motion passed unanimously
